This surah is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah the Exalted says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), bestowing favour upon him: ﴿Indeed, We have granted you al-Kawthar﴾; that is, abundant good and vast bounty. Among its parts is what Allah gives His Prophet (ﷺ) on the Day of Resurrection: the river called al-Kawthar, and the Basin (al-Hawd), whose length is a month's journey and whose breadth is a month's journey. Its water is whiter than milk and sweeter than honey, and its vessels are as numerous as the stars of the sky in their quantity and their brightness. Whoever drinks from it a single draught will never thirst after it, ever.

{2} When He had mentioned His favour upon him, He commanded him to give thanks for it, saying: ﴿So pray to your Lord and sacrifice﴾. He singled out these two acts of worship for mention because they are the most excellent of acts of worship and the most exalted of acts of drawing near to Allah. Prayer includes humility of the heart and the limbs before Allah, and it moves the worshipper through various kinds of servitude. In sacrifice (al-nahr) there is a drawing near to Allah with the finest of the animals a servant possesses, and a giving out of wealth, which souls are naturally inclined to love and to be miserly with.

{3} ﴿Indeed, your enemy﴾; that is, the one who hates you, reviles you and belittles you, ﴿is the one cut off (al-abtar)﴾; that is, the one cut off from every good: cut off in deed and cut off in remembrance. As for Muhammad (ﷺ), he is complete in truth, possessing the perfection attainable for a created being: the elevation of his remembrance and the abundance of his helpers and followers (ﷺ).
